# Minimized fuzz failures

Each file here is the smallest input found for one failure of a fuzz target of
`tools/MetadataSharp.Fuzz`, filed under the target that found it. They are authored for this
repository (written byte by byte from the failure, or minimized by `afl-tmin` from an input the
campaign built); none is a copy of a third-party file.

`tests/MetadataSharp.Tests/Fuzz/FuzzRegressionTests.cs` runs every file of `tests/fixtures` through
every target on every platform and framework, so each failure stays fixed. A failure is an exception
other than a `MetadataException` with a defined code, a broken invariant of the harness, or a hang.

| File | Target | What it found | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `write/jpeg-comment-with-zero-byte.jpg` | write | A comment holding a zero byte reads as U+0000, which a written comment cannot hold: `MetadataOperations.CopyMetadata` and `InsertExv` threw `ArgumentException` (first seen on four exiv2 CRW test files). | The comment is left behind with a note; the rest is copied. |
| `write/jpeg-photoshop-block-split-across-app13.jpg` | write | A Photoshop resource block split across two APP13 segments reads in the JPEG file, but the EXV file `ExtractExv` made from it did not: the EXV reader parsed each segment alone (first seen on three exiv2 `iptc-psAPP13s-*` files). | The EXV reader joins the Photoshop segments as the JPEG reader does. |
| `write/webp-exif-and-xmp-in-one-save.webp` | write | `SaveAll` of a WebP file with an EXIF and an XMP change kept the XMP change and dropped the EXIF one; a BMFF file dropped the XMP one (the owned `b7` files reproduce that). | Both documents apply the EXIF edit, then the XMP edit on its output, each verified. |
| `previews/raf-jpeg-with-unreadable-exif.raf` | previews | Found while triaging the container refusals the previews target reported for the CRW, MRW and RAF test files of exiv2: `Previews.List` of a RAF file also threw what the EXIF reader of its embedded JPEG refused, although the previews depend only on the header. | The listing collects the refusals of the metadata readers and lists the previews. |
| `stream/tail-starts-like-jpeg-xl.bin`, `stream/tail-starts-like-jpeg-2000.bin`, `stream/tail-starts-like-tiff.bin` | stream | A read from a stream or a path tested the last 26 bytes against every signature, where only a TARGA footer belongs: a file whose tail began like a JPEG XL codestream, a JPEG 2000 box or a TIFF header was read as that format there and as an unknown one from memory. | The tail is tested for the TARGA footer alone, in the library and in `tools/MetadataSharp.Dump`. |
| `write/tiff-iptc-with-unparseable-resources.tiff` | write | A TIFF whose IPTC is tag 0x83BB and whose Photoshop image resources (tag 0x8649, stored as LONGs) do not parse lost its IPTC when it was deleted, and the reader then reported an IPTC error for the resources the source still held (first seen in run 43692079077). | When the whole IPTC is removed, the IPTC resource and its digest are removed from the resources tag as well - every other resource kept, the framing rebuilt, the tag deleted when nothing remains - and resources that do not parse, are not stored as bytes or fail validation are refused with a code, not written. |
| `stream/bmff-ftyp-crash-not-reproduced.bmff` | stream | In run 43727822510 afl-fuzz saved one crash after 49.5 s (268,459 executions) of the same 9,784-byte BMFF file that opens with `ftyp`, with only byte 149 set to 0x01 instead of 0x00; replayed alone it passes in 67 ms. | Not reproduced; the same asynchronous sig 2 as the `write` input, which this file differs from in one byte. The input is filed so every platform keeps running it. |
| `write/bmff-ftyp-crash-not-reproduced.bmff` | write | In run 43696038465 afl-fuzz saved one crash after 274.6 s (375,924 executions) of a BMFF file that opens with `ftyp`; replayed alone it passes, and 40,000 mutated executions in one process under the 512 MiB heap limit kept the retained heap at 0.6 MiB. The minimized form (9,784 bytes) is in that run's annotations. | Not reproduced; sig 2 is an asynchronous signal to the process, not a fault the input raises. The input is filed so every platform keeps running it. |
| `write/bmff-ftyp-crash-not-reproduced-2.bmff` | write | In run 43730432167 (the pull request) afl-fuzz saved one crash after 84 s (167,272 executions) of another 9,784-byte BMFF file that opens with `ftyp` (3,737 bytes different from the run-43696038465 input); replayed alone it passes in 217 ms. | Not reproduced; sig 2 is an asynchronous signal to the process, not a fault the input raises. The input is filed so every platform keeps running it. |
| `write/bmff-meta-hdlr-crash-not-reproduced.bmff` | write | In run 43728882787 afl-fuzz saved one crash (src 000075) after 263.9 s (358,003 executions) of a smaller BMFF file that opens with `ftyp`, then `meta` and `hdlr` (765 bytes, big-endian int16 at byte 132); replayed alone it passes in 212 ms. The same seed saved the same crash again in run 43732008055, at byte 131 (one byte different from this file) and at byte 145 (241 bytes different); both replayed in 13 and 182 ms. Every occurrence is the same asynchronous sig 2 near the same field; they are filed once, here. | Not reproduced; sig 2 is an asynchronous signal to the process, not a fault the input raises. The input is filed so every platform keeps running it. |
| `write/mrw-entry-of-unknown-field-type.mrw` | write | An entry of a field type TIFF 6.0 does not define is read one byte per element; `CopyMetadata` carried it into an `ExifEdit`, whose writer threw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` converting its byte order. | `ExifEdit.Set` and `SetUnchecked` refuse such a value with the documented `ArgumentException`, which the copy turns into a note; see `ExifEditTests`. |
